newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers announce special panel to 'save' Amtrak.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers announce special panel to 'save' Amtrak.

text.p: Leading Republicans and Democrats on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee announced on Thursday that a special committee of experts would be formed to chart ways to save Amtrak.
"Without decisive action very soon, the country will have no inter-city rail service within a few months," said committee chairman Bud Shuster, a Pennsylvania Republican.

He said it was evident from testimony by Amtrak and the General Accounting Office, the Congressional watchdog agency, that even under optimistic estimates Amtrak could not survive through the next financial year that starts on October 1.
Shuster said the national passenger railroad was already borrowing money to meet payroll costs and it will exhaust all available lines of credit by the middle of 1998.
He said the panel, whose members would be named soon, would try to come up with original ideas to form the basis of a bipartisan legislative solution to Amtrak's financial problems.

Joining Shuster in support for the Blue Ribbon panel were the committee's senior Democrat, James Oberstar of Minnesota; the chairman of its railroads subcommittee, Susan Molinari, a New York Republican, and the subcommittee's top Democrat, Robert Wise of West Virginia.
